question: What is lenacapavir, and what did the US FDA approve it for in 2025?
text:
Lenacapavir is a long-acting antiretroviral drug that blocks the HIV-1 capsid, the protein shell the virus needs to replicate. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/220020s000lbl.pdf?utm_source=openai))

On **June 18, 2025**, the U.S. FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name **Yeztugo** as **pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)** to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV-1 through sex. It was approved for at-risk adults and adolescents who weigh at least 35 kg (77 lb) and test negative for HIV-1 before starting. After the starting doses, it’s given as an injection every six months. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/220020Orig1s000Approv.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The 2025 approval was for **prevention**. The FDA had already approved lenacapavir in 2022 as **Sunlenca**, used with other antiretrovirals to treat certain adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/220018Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf?utm_source=openai))
